 Hon'Ble Jitendra Kumar Sinha, J. 
1.

Heard Sri Atmaran Nadiwal, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Manoj Gautam, learned
A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.

3. The present application has been moved seeking anticipatory bail in Case Crime no. 459 of 2022
under sections 419, 420, 467, 468, 471 and 120B Ipc, Police Station Nichlaul, District Maharajganj
with the prayer that in the event of arrest, the applicant may be released on bail.

4.  It has been contended by learned counsel for the applicant that applicant is not named in the FIR and per the FIR, co-accused Vijay Verma is said to have executed a sale deed in favour of the first informant by impersonation.

He further submits that co-accused Vijay Verma has already been enlarged on anticipatory bail by Co-ordinate Bench of this Court vide order dated 23.6.2025 passed in Crl. Misc. Anticipatory Bail Application No. 4113 of 2025.

entities.text: Crl. Misc. Anticipatory Bail Application No. 4113 of 2025
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: It is further submitted that other co-accused persons have also been enlarged on anticipatory bail.
It is further submitted that applicant has no criminal history to his credit.

It was also submitted that applicant undertakes to co-operate during trial and he would appear as and when required by the investigating agency or Court and in case he is granted anticipatory bail, he shall not misuse the liberty of bail and would obey all conditions of bail.
5.
On the other hand, learned A.G.A. has opposed the prayer for grant of anticipatory bail and submits that applicant is marginal witness to the alleged sale deed.
6. I have considered the rival submissions made by learned counsel for the parties.
7. Applicant is not named in the FIR and as per the FIR, co-accused Vijay Verma is said to have executed a sale deed in favour of the first informant by impersonation.

Co-accused Vijay Verma has already been enlarged on anticipatory bail by Co-ordinate Bench of this Court and other co-accused persons have also been enlarged on anticipatory bail by Co-ordinate Bench of this Court.
Applicant has no criminal history to his credit.

8. It may be stated that in case of Siddharam Satlingappa Mhetre v. State of Maharashtra, (2011) 1 SCC 694, it has been held by Hon'ble Supreme Court that while deciding anticipatory bail, the Court must consider nature and gravity of accusation, antecedents of the accused, possibility of accused to flee from justice and that Court must evaluate the entire available material against the accused carefully and the exact role of accused has also to be taken into consideration.
9.

entities.text: Siddharam Satlingappa Mhetre v. State of Maharashtra, (2011) 1 SCC 694
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In the instant case, considering the settled principle of law regarding anticipatory bail,
submissions of learned counsel for the parties, nature of accusation, role of applicant and all attending facts and circumstances of the case, without expressing any opinion on merits, a case for anticipatory bail is made out.
10. The anticipatory bail application is allowed.

opennyai_summary.decision:
In the instant case, considering the settled principle of law regarding anticipatory bail,
submissions of learned counsel for the parties, nature of accusation, role of applicant and all attending facts and circumstances of the case, without expressing any opinion on merits, a case for anticipatory bail is made out.
10. The anticipatory bail application is allowed.
In the event of arrest of the applicant Manthan Prajapati involved in the aforesaid case crime, he shall be released on anticipatory bail on his furnishing a personal bond of Rs. 50,000/- with two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Court concerned, with the following conditions :-
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with evidence and that he would appear before the trial Court on the date fixed unless exempted by the Court concerned;
(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him/her/them from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer;
(iii) The applicant would co-operate during trial and would not misuse the liberty of bail.
(iv) The applicant shall not leave India without prior permission of the Court concerned.
12. In default of any of the conditions, the prosecution shall be at liberty to file appropriate application for cancellation of anticipatory bail granted to the applicant.
